title: Implement graceful shutdown with in‑flight request handling
description: Adds a production‑ready shutdown sequence that stops accepting new connections, waits for ongoing requests to finish, and then closes the server. This prevents dropped requests during deployments or crashes and improves reliability.
testCases: Verify that new connections are rejected after shutdown is initiated
Verify that existing requests complete successfully before the process exits
acceptance: When the shutdown endpoint or SIGTERM is triggered, the server stops accepting new connections, waits up to a configurable timeout for active requests to finish, then exits with code 0. If the timeout elapses, pending requests are terminated and the process exits with code 1. All logs reflect each step of the shutdown process.
reason: Production deployments and auto‑scaling require reliable termination to avoid 5xx errors. A graceful shutdown feature eliminates request loss, improves uptime metrics, and aligns yantraverse with enterprise‑grade expectations.
